summary: Independently re-verified all 3 run.sh files, the test file, and all evidence logs from scratch. The save/restore/unset bash logic in skills/self/spawn/run.sh, skills/self/spawn-child/run.sh, and skills/economy/lending/run.sh is byte-identical and correctly implemented (implementation_correctness PASSES on positive evidence). However: (1) REQ-003's claim to have found every duplicate of the vulnerable preamble is false -- an independent repo-wide grep finds a 4th, never-mentioned instance in skills/anicca-life-manager/scripts/wake_event_ensure.sh:14 (FIND-001, spec_fidelity FAIL); (2) REQ-001's own documented 'no ANICCA_HOME set' edge case has zero test coverage -- both test cases in run-sh-anicca-home-preservation.test.mjs always set ANICCA_HOME (FIND-002, edge_case_coverage FAIL); (3) PROP-006's claimed proof for economy/lending/run.sh and self/spawn-child/run.sh rests on a purely static-text regex test (wake-gate-structural.test.mjs:44) that would pass identically against the ORIGINAL vulnerable code, and self/spawn-child has no run.sh test at all -- only self/spawn/run.sh has genuine subprocess-executing regression protection (FIND-003, verification_readiness FAIL); (4) the fix is hand-copied into 3 separate files with no shared source of truth, which is the direct structural cause of both iteration-3's original propagation gap and this iteration's newly-found 4th instance (FIND-004, structural_integrity FAIL). The economy/lending 130/131 test result's single failure (PROP-117a, a stray .worktrees/ceo-loop copy of wake-gate.mjs) was independently confirmed real and plausibly unrelated to this feature's changes (the failing assertion concerns lending-orchestrator.mjs call-site counting, not run.sh's env preamble), and the .worktrees/ceo-loop directory was confirmed to exist on disk.
